title: Three Months and One Short Chair
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：string　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 string 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the father ① tied the string that no neighbour in the house would have counted, and he said the tying was the whole of the month. The ② string, meaning the cord itself and not the chair, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a string, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ string in that house had the same short chair beside it, and the ④ string at the far door, meaning the box they kept for the children to carry and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A string, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the father said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the string was the whole of the matter, meaning the connection and not the cord. The ⑥ string, meaning the connection and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; string, he said, is either something you tie or the only word that means both a cord and a connection. He said the connection is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ string had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short chair. The ⑧ string of the whole thing, the father wrote in September, was one house and three months of counting; string, he said, is either the box at the far door or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ string I remember is the cord counted in the letter, which closed in 1968 and is still counted as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ string, my mother said in 1970, is the only cord that improves by being counted; every string, she said, is a connection that has agreed to look like a cord. She said the connection was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 细绳；一串（指老屋里每一根旁边的那一根）
B. n. 细绳；一串（指那根细绳本身，与小小的板凳相对）
C. 固定搭配：tie the string 系这一根细绳
D. n. 细绳；一串（指留给孩子们搬的那一只）
E. n. 细绳之事（抽象总称，指一处老屋的细绳之事）
F. n. 细绳；一串（指家书里写到、被清点的那一根）
G. n. 细绳、牵连（指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 牵连（抽象总称，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: tied the string that no neighbour in the house would have counted
The string, meaning the cord itself and not the chair
the string at the far door
the string was the whole of the matter
the string had become a line in a letter
The string of the whole thing
A string, my mother said in 1970

answers.why: tie the string 意为“系这一根细绳”，1961 年那位父亲把老屋里没有一位邻居肯清点的一根细绳做了一遍。
string 意为“细绳；一串”，指那根细绳本身而不是小小的板凳，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
string 意为“细绳；一串”，指老屋里每一根旁边的那一根，每一根旁边都有同一张小小的板凳。
string 意为“细绳；一串”，指最远那道门口的留给孩子们搬的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
string 意为“细绳、牵连”，指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这根牵连就是那件事的全部。
string 意为“牵连”，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西而不是那根细绳，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
string 意为“细绳；一串”，指家书里写到、被清点的那一根，到 1966 年这一根成了家书里的一行。
string 意为“细绳之事”，父亲九月写道，整件事的细绳之事是一处老屋和三个月份的清点。
string 意为“细绳；一串”，我记得的是家书里清点过的那一根，1968 年搬完了，至今仍被说成老屋里最安静的一根。
string 为抽象总称，母亲 1970 年说，细绳是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的细绳。
